Date: 2026-07-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: header propagation option for Private SDK (Brightlane PoC)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We pushed the PoC to our staging Private deployment this morning and hit a blocker: our upstream LB rewrites the caller-id headers (X-Caller-Id, X-Request-Id) and Redwood's SDK/runtime stack isn't preserving the original headers when requests are proxied into our VPC. That breaks user identity propagation for our downstream services.

Can you confirm whether there is a config toggle we can flip on the Private deployment or SDK to preserve inbound headers through the Redwood control plane/gateway? If not, can your team recommend a short-term workaround while we evaluate the PoC?

I've attached a small capture from our staging gateway (brightlane_poc_logs.txt) showing the incoming vs forwarded headers.

Thanks,
Emma Carter
Head of Integrations | Brightlane
emma@brightlane.com

Thanks Naomi. Quick notes from Sales Eng perspective after a fast read of the logs:

- This looks like a header whitelist at the gateway/control-plane boundary for Private deployments. If we strip by default for security, that's expected.
- Short-term workaround for Brightlane: ask them to set a route hint header (x-redwood-route) and/or embed caller identity in the request body payload (JSON.metadata.caller_id) so downstream services can use it. That's not ideal.
- Ideally we expose a per-deployment flag (opt-in) to preserve a set of inbound headers, with a guardrail for headers that could cause routing/control-plane confusion.

Can Platform/runtime confirm feasibility and rough ETA? If this requires a code change, we should also scope SOC/Compliance signoff impacts for Private customers.

Logan Wright
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: header propagation option for Private SDK (Brightlane PoC)

Hey all — looked into the logs and the flow. Summary:

- Root cause: the private control plane enforces a header whitelist and normalizes X-Caller-Id / X-Request-Id for safety; incoming headers are dropped unless explicitly allowed. That whitelist is intentional for hosted tenants, and for Private deployments it's a conservative default.
- Feasibility: we can add an opt-in config flag on the Private control plane called "preserve_inbound_headers" which accepts an allowlist. Runtime impact: small (gateway pass-through path), but we need tests around replayability and header canonicalization.
- Risk: certain headers can affect routing decisions; we must disallow headers that mutate our internal routing (e.g., x-redwood-route) unless combined with a validation policy.

Short proposal attached: rfc-preserve-headers-draft.md — includes API surface (control-plane toggle + per-deployment allowlist), telemetry additions, and a plan for canary rollout behind feature flag.

As a short-term mitigation we can add a translation layer in the SDK that moves caller_id into a signed metadata token that the control plane will preserve. That would be an SDK change and might be faster for Brightlane to adopt while we implement the control-plane toggle.

Marissa Cole
Staff Platform Engineer, Runtime
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: rfc-preserve-headers-draft.md

Subject: RE: Request: header propagation option for Private SDK (Brightlane PoC)

Emma — quick status update for Brightlane:

- We confirmed the cause (private control plane header whitelist).
- Platform has proposed a config toggle (preserve_inbound_headers) with a per-deployment allowlist; they're drafting an RFC and can scope work.
- Short-term workaround: if you can include caller identity in request body (metadata.caller_id) or set a signed token in a header (we can provide SDK helper to sign), downstream services can consume without waiting for control-plane changes.

If you can send one example request (raw headers + body) from staging and the failing request-id, Marissa asked to attach a sample so they can reproduce locally.

Next steps: Platform will produce an ETA on the RFC and a short runbook for enabling the toggle. I'll coordinate with Procurement once we have an estimated timeline for a Private deployment fix.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: header propagation option for Private SDK (Brightlane PoC) — triage plan

Team — proposed triage/rollout plan:

1) Short-term (1 week): provide Brightlane an SDK helper to encode caller identity in a signed header (x-rw-caller-sig). This avoids control-plane changes and is low effort for Sales Eng + SDK.
2) Mid-term (3–5 weeks): implement control-plane flag preserve_inbound_headers with per-deployment allowlist. Implementation plan: feature-flagged gateway pass-through path, unit/integration tests, and docs.
3) Canary: start with Brightlane + 1 other Private customer in us-west, monitor INF-telemetry for header replay and routing anomalies.
4) Docs & Compliance: update Private deployment security guide and run a compliance review for header preservation policy.

I created a Jira: INF-4532 and linked a HubSpot card HS-7821 for the deal. Patch branch and test-plan sketches attached (patch-branch-link.txt, test-plan.md).

Question for Naomi/procurement: will Brightlane require an SLA or contractual language change to allow header passthrough? If so, loop in Legal.

If everyone agrees I'll queue the SDK helper as a high-priority patch and start the RFC review for the control-plane toggle.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
